description:

definitionOfDone: A production call path delivers a real launch result into createFoundationAttemptService's captureResult port — zero non-test implementations becomes at least one, verified by grep and a real-store test through the production path
Every captured field traces to the launch result or durable records — a hostile arm proves caller-supplied result bytes are refused or ignored with the exact code

Owned-package gates run separately, exit 0, printed nonzero counts

=== TWO MEASUREMENTS THAT BREAK THE PLAN'S STEP-3 FLOW ===

1. THE PRELAUNCH PROOF IS NOT DURABLE. foundation-capture-lifecycle.ts:84-86 states it and the record proves it: PreparedCapture.proof is FoundationPrelaunchProof|null and is null on REPLAYED; contextCandidate (:213-226) writes baselineDigest = manifest.sha256, NOT the proof digest. FOUNDATION_CAPTURE_CONTEXT_KEYS has no proof field. scannedEntryCount/scannedByteTotal exist nowhere durable.

2. RE-PROVING POST-LAUNCH REFUSES, on exactly the arm the DoD makes mandatory. proveFoundationPrelaunchTree -> scanDeclaredTrees -> scannedTreeRejection (foundation-workspace-capture-rules.ts:50-71) requires the scanned tree to EQUAL the sealed input entries: a newly authored file returns RUNNER_FOUNDATION_CAPTURE_INPUT_ENTRY_EXTRA, a modified one INPUT_ENTRY_CHANGED. So step-3's "prelaunch equality proof against the record's sealed manifest, then postlaunch delta" cannot run after a launch that authored anything.

AND THE OBVIOUS WORKAROUND IS DELIBERATELY LOCKED. Sealing a proof from the record is impossible from the daemon: `sealPrelaunchProof` is WITHHELD from @moe/runner's public surface. Measured, not read — the first probe failed with `error TS2305: Module '"@moe/runner"' has no exported member 'sealPrelaunchProof'`, and packages/runner/src/index.ts:315-330 gives the rationale verbatim: "sealPrelaunchProof MINTS the proof ... A consumer able to call either could hand this package a fabricated 'the tree was proven'." A root-barrel grep alone would have missed this — the symbol appears in index.ts (line 324) only inside that comment.

CONSEQUENCE, carried into steps 2-4 and recorded as a comment on the row: the proof must travel LEXICALLY from prepared.proof to the producer, the same discipline captureRef already uses and for the same reason. That needs a 7th key on the captureResult call-site input in foundation-attempt-service.ts (an owned file in this plan's step-1 affectedFiles, but one planningNotes risk 4 asked me to leave untouched). It does not weaken the caller-smuggling bar — the proof, like captureRef, comes from THIS dispatch's own preparation and can never come from a caller. Alternatives rejected: re-prove post-launch (refuses, above), mint the proof locally (withheld by design), persist it in the record (edits the closed record key list + digest of freshly QA-approved bytes, far larger blast radius).

implementationPlan.description: PARALLEL/REPLAY ISOLATION — the lesson from f146fa2e's QA reject (reopen 1) baked in: the parallel arms use DISTINCT identities (distinct attemptId AND distinct aggregate/session so the reservation cannot dedup) and assert DISTINCT captureRefs, DISTINCT worktree roots, and DISTINCT results read back from the store; two identical requests asserting refs.size===1 is a dedup control, not a non-crossing proof — that exact shape let a module-global sticky-ref mutant survive 3492 green tests one task ago. REPLAY: re-delivery of the SAME command returns the same durable answer WITHOUT a rescan — prove no-rescan physically: mutate a file in the worktree between first delivery and replay, assert the replayed answer's bytes are UNCHANGED (a rescan would see the mutation); count store rows to prove no second decision.
implementationPlan.note:
PARALLEL + REPLAY ISOLATION. Producer suite 25 passed (25), 37.52s. Service suite 66 passed (66), 26.90s. Typecheck clean.

PARALLEL, with f146fa2e's reject lesson applied rather than restated. Both arms carry DISTINCT identities (attemptId attempt-1/attempt-2, aggregate agg-producer-1/2, session session-1/2, and distinct request+reservation digests) over ONE SHARED STORE, so a module-global is genuinely reachable rather than partitioned away by separate fixtures. Distinctness of captureRef and of assignment.realWorktreePath is asserted BEFORE any capture runs, or the rest of the case would be comparing one dispatch with itself.

The assertion is deliberately NOT a set-size check. Each tree is authored with DIFFERENT bytes and each answer's alpha digest is asserted to be its OWN tree's sha256 by value — `one -> digest(ALPHA)`, `two -> digest(BETA)` — so a SWAP fails. `refs.size === 2` passes a swap; distinctness is not identity, which is exactly the correction qa-bbdecc14 landed on the sibling task. The untouched declared sibling is additionally asserted byte-IDENTICAL across both answers, so the difference above is pinned to the authored path rather than to two unrelated scans.

CROSSING ARM, same shared store: this dispatch's identifiers against the other dispatch's captureRef AND proof together — both real, both honestly sealed — refuses FOUNDATION_CAPTURE_PRODUCER_IDENTITY_MISMATCH @ DAEMON_FOUNDATION_CAPTURE. Paired with a POSITIVE CONTROL in the same case (the same producer, same store, uncrossed, answers with authoredPaths [scope/alpha.txt]), because a producer that refused everything would satisfy the refusal assertion alone.

REPLAY / NO RESCAN, proved PHYSICALLY at the durable row where replay actually happens. The producer is not the replay layer — dispatch() short-circuits a re-delivery on the stored attempt row and never reaches capture() — so the property is pinned there: after the authored settlement, the worktree file is rewritten with different bytes, the row is read again, and the sealed resultManifest sha256 is byte-identical. Anything that re-scanned would see the new bytes; "it answered quickly" would have proved nothing. Event types on the dispatch aggregate are captured before and asserted equal after, so no second decision was written, and the before-count is asserted nonzero so an empty list cannot satisfy the comparison vacuously.

TWO MORE PROPERTIES PINNED, both cheap and both easy to break by accident:
- The producer WRITES NOTHING DURABLE: the capture aggregate's event count is unchanged after two answers (with the before-count asserted nonzero). This is load-bearing for the replay path above, which assumes capture has no side effect of its own.
- The producer RE-SCANS rather than caching: authoring twice yields two different digests, and the second is asserted to be the sha256 of the second write. A cached answer would report a tree that no longer exists — the same class of lie as trusting caller-supplied result bytes. Stated in the test's own comment so the two behaviours (row replays, producer re-scans) are not confused later.
